title: Chai at 3:07, Ep 1: The Stall That Wasn't There
logline: A tea stall appears on a mountain highway at 3:07 every night. Everyone who stops there is about to die on the road, and tonight it's Kabir's turn.
trend_basis: Local horror tied to a real kind of place: haunted highway stories (811K) and festival ghost stories (4.5M) lead this week's scan
Series labelling and cliffhanger titles outperform the scan median
Micro-dramas of about a minute are found through feeds; few horror channels use that format
original_twist: The haunted stall is the only safe place on the road. Its ghost is trying to save the living, and each episode Kabir must keep one doomed stranger from driving away before 3:08.

series.title: Chai at 3:07
series.season_arc: Kabir learns why the stall chose him, and who Noor was before the road took her.
series.cliffhanger: Kabir's own truck drives past the stall with Kabir at the wheel, heading for the broken bridge.

story.opening_hook: A dashboard clock flips to 3:07 and a lit tea stall appears in the fog where there was only cliff a second ago.

acts.name: Hook
acts.summary: The stall appears out of nothing at 3:07.

acts.name: Warning
acts.summary: Noor already has Kabir's tea poured and tells him not to leave before 3:08.

acts.name: Proof
acts.summary: He laughs it off, walks back toward his truck, and sees it drive past with himself inside.

story.ending: Kabir stands frozen at the stall holding the glass as his own truck's tail lights vanish toward the broken bridge. Noor says only: 'Now you believe me.'

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, film grain, night on a foggy Himalayan mountain highway, cold blue moonlight with warm orange lantern glow. Kabir, a 45-year-old Indian truck driver with a thick grey-streaked beard, a deep crease between his brows, wearing a faded maroon turban, a brown wool shawl over a khaki shirt climbs down from the cab of a painted Indian cargo truck and walks warily toward a small tin-roofed roadside tea stall lit by a single lantern. shots.voiceover: Kabir: Twenty years on this road. There was never a stall here.

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, film grain, night on a foggy Himalayan mountain highway, cold blue moonlight with warm orange lantern glow. Medium close-up of Noor, a 20-year-old Indian woman with a long single black braid, a small silver nose stud, pale grey eyes, wearing a dark green salwar kameez and a mustard yellow shawl standing behind the wooden counter of a tin-roofed tea stall, steam rising from a kettle. She slides a glass of chai forward without looking down and says softly: "Your tea, Kabir. Two sugars. Do not leave before 3:08." Her face is calm, lantern light on one side.
shots.dialogue: Noor: Your tea, Kabir. Two sugars. Do not leave before 3:08.

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, film grain, night on a foggy Himalayan mountain highway, cold blue moonlight with warm orange lantern glow. Medium close-up of Kabir, a 45-year-old Indian truck driver with a thick grey-streaked beard, a deep crease between his brows, wearing a faded maroon turban, a brown wool shawl over a khaki shirt at the counter of a tin-roofed tea stall, holding a small glass of chai. He frowns, then gives a short disbelieving laugh and says: "How do you know my name, girl? I have a delivery to make." He turns his head toward the road.
